combinations.description: Copy a working arrangement, raise local capacity around it, and map the domain first.
combinations.name: Seed + Raise + Map

combinations.description: Probe with bounded experiments, then prove at pilot scale before committing.
combinations.name: Probe + Prove

combinations.description: Frame the gap, observe the region, and model it before any intervention moves.
combinations.name: Frame + Observe + Map

combinations.description: Align incentives, then verify the alignment held with independent evaluation.
combinations.name: Align + Verify

description: Synthetic seed dataset for the Atlas of State Action. Provisional hand-authored rows in the Instrument / Intervention element schemas; eventually generated from the notes corpus.

interventions.description: Seed a missing productive capability by copying a working foreign arrangement into the local region, then adapting it.
interventions.name: Structured Imitation & Capability Seeding
interventions.problem: A region lacks a productive capability that exists elsewhere; inventing from scratch is slow and risky.

interventions.description: Build the institutional capacity to absorb, adapt, and improve imported techniques rather than merely operating them.
interventions.name: Absorptive Capacity & Institutional Learning
interventions.problem: Imported technology stalls because local institutions cannot absorb or adapt it.

interventions.description: Shift from imitation to autonomy by granting research freedom and tolerating failure inside funded missions.
interventions.name: Innovation Culture & Autonomy Transition
interventions.problem: A top-down agenda suppresses the autonomous exploration that breakthroughs require.

interventions.description: Nurture latent local potential by finding and removing the binding constraint, letting growth emerge from within.
interventions.name: Bottleneck Removal (Inductionism)
interventions.problem: Growth is blocked by one binding constraint, but interventions spray effort everywhere.

interventions.description: Replace an inefficient arrangement by intentionally building new rules, roles, and organizations.
interventions.name: Institutional Design (Constructivism)
interventions.problem: Existing rules and organizations reproduce the undesired outcome; tweaks cannot escape them.

interventions.description: Reshape individual choices through prices and rewards so decentralized agents coordinate toward the goal.
interventions.name: Incentive Reform (Atomism)
interventions.problem: Agents' private interests diverge from the collective objective; commands are unenforceable.

interventions.description: Break a stuck pattern with a bounded shock — a demonstration, challenge, or pilot — forcing adaptation.
interventions.name: Pattern-Breaking Pilot (Disruptivism)
interventions.problem: An arrangement is locked in a local optimum; incremental moves cannot dislodge it.

interventions.description: Align behavior by shaping shared norms and values through education and culture rather than enforcement.
interventions.name: Norm Shaping (Normativism)
interventions.problem: Formal rules exist but behavior follows contrary informal norms.

interventions.description: Translate a strategic selection into an ordered, sponsored set of initiatives with milestones.
interventions.name: Agenda-Led Mobilization
interventions.problem: Many worthy objectives compete; without an ordering, effort fragments.

interventions.description: Bind separately managed projects under one objective, budget envelope, and governance.
interventions.name: Program Commitment
interventions.problem: Isolated projects duplicate effort and evade joint accountability.

instruments.description: Turn complex realities into actionable problems by interrogating assumptions and framing the gap between what is and what ought to be.
instruments.name: Problematization

instruments.description: Design rewards, penalties, and recognition so strategic agents choose actions aligned with the collective objective.
instruments.name: Mechanism Design

instruments.description: Observe, measure, and register social reality from an explicit external position, localizing reflexivity.
instruments.name: External Observation

instruments.description: Build formal representations — models, maps, schemas — that compress a domain for reasoning and simulation.
instruments.name: Modelling

instruments.description: Assess performance and effectiveness against criteria: competitiveness, wealth, social accounting.
instruments.name: Evaluation

instruments.description: Plan, conduct, and analyze bounded experiments to discriminate between candidate explanations.
instruments.name: Experimental Design

instruments.description: Raise productive capacity in place: digital transformation, extension, quality indexes.
instruments.name: Upgrading

instruments.description: Test and validate new technologies at small scale before full implementation, crossing the valley of death.
instruments.name: Pilot Plant
